title: When anger takes over
issueStatement: The body is already hot and the mind is already arguing its case. Hurt, pride, and urgency have begun calling themselves truth.
centralInsight: Gurbani treats anger as fire that consumes discernment. The answer is not denial but cooling through humility, softened speech, and conquest of the mind.
practicalReflection: Anger promises strength while quietly handing the self over to impulse. What feels like power in the moment often leaves the heart smaller afterward.
actionPrompt: Before the next hard reply, give the heat one line of Naam and one breath more than it wants.
searchTerms: training anger into a smaller first response

source.shortMeaning: Ego is a chronic disease, but it contains its own cure as well; where does ego come from? How can it be removed
source.lifeApplication: Slow the tongue before you defend the self-image behind it. Let the line stay in charge of what comes next.

excerpts.explanation: Anger is not handled here as a separate weather system. The shabad pushes below the flare-up and shows the ego underneath it asking to rule the moment.

source.shortMeaning: Her speech is sweet, and her way of life is humble. She enjoys the Bed of her Husband Lord; chant the Name of the Lord, and find peace
source.lifeApplication: Slow the tongue before you defend the self-image behind it. Let the line stay in charge of what comes next.

excerpts.explanation: The correction to anger is concrete. Sweet speech and humble conduct are not niceness theatre; they are evidence that the inner fire has begun to cool.

source.shortMeaning: Make contentment your ear-rings, humility your begging bowl, and meditation the ashes you apply to your body; see the brotherhood of all mankind as the highest order of Yogis

excerpts.explanation: The real victory is moved inward. Anger loses some of its glamour the moment the struggle is understood as mastery of the mind rather than mastery of the room.

repair.practicalReflection: Repair becomes honest when the mind stops turning failure into identity and lets the next true act matter.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: Training anger into a smaller first response
practice.issueStatement: Anger is not weakened by one clear realization. It keeps returning through pace, pride, and the habit of treating heat as authority.
practice.centralInsight: Gurbani trains anger by cooling the inner field first. Humility, conquered speech, and remembrance make reaction less believable as truth.
practice.practicalReflection: A peaceful life is not built by waiting for fewer provocations. It is built by practicing a smaller first movement when the provocation arrives.
practice.actionPrompt: Choose one recurring trigger this week and rehearse a slower, softer first sentence there until anger stops feeling automatic.
